topics.label: Beyond GDP: why and how to measure social welfare
topics.summary: The case against GDP as a welfare measure and the main alternatives: dashboards, capabilities, and consumption-equivalent welfare.

claims.title: Report by the Commission on the Measurement of Economic Performance and Social Progress
claims.venue: Commission on the Measurement of Economic Performance and Social Progress
claims.rationale: The canonical statement of the beyond-GDP agenda: why GDP fails as a welfare measure and what dashboards of well-being, quality of life, and sustainability should contain.

claims.title: Beyond GDP: The Quest for a Measure of Social Welfare
claims.rationale: Surveys the theoretical options (corrected GDP, synthetic indicators, equivalent income, subjective well-being) and the normative trade-offs each makes.

claims.title: Beyond GDP? Welfare across Countries and Time
claims.rationale: A welfare-theoretic alternative to composite indices: a single consumption-equivalent metric that reorders countries relative to GDP; useful contrast with ad hoc aggregation.

topics.label: Constructing composite indicators: normalisation, weighting, aggregation
topics.summary: The standard methodology for building composite indices and the critiques of its arbitrary choices.

claims.title: Handbook on Constructing Composite Indicators: Methodology and User Guide
claims.rationale: The reference manual for the ten-step pipeline (framework, data, imputation, normalisation, weighting, aggregation, robustness) used by most published indices.

claims.title: On the Methodological Framework of Composite Indices: A Review of the Issues of Weighting, Aggregation, and Robustness
claims.rationale: Recent review of weighting and aggregation schemes, compensability, and sensitivity analysis; a map of the methodological literature since the OECD handbook.

claims.title: Mashup Indices of Development
claims.rationale: Sharp critique of composite indices whose weights lack a theoretical basis; shows how implicit trade-offs between components can be absurd.

claims.title: Weights in Multidimensional Indices of Wellbeing: An Overview
claims.rationale: Classifies weighting approaches (data-driven, normative, hybrid) and makes explicit the marginal rates of substitution a weight vector implies.

topics.label: Worked cases: the HDI and multidimensional poverty indices
topics.summary: Two heavily scrutinised composite indices that illustrate the construction choices and their controversies in practice.

claims.title: Counting and multidimensional poverty measurement
claims.rationale: The axiomatic dual-cutoff method behind the global MPI; the clearest example of a composite index built from explicit identification and aggregation axioms.

claims.title: The HDI 2010: new controversies, old critiques
claims.rationale: Explains the 2010 switch to geometric aggregation in the HDI and responds to critiques about substitutability and implicit trade-offs.

claims.title: On multidimensional indices of poverty
claims.rationale: Argues for dashboards over single multidimensional indices; the direct counterpoint to Alkire-Foster in the same debate.

topics.label: Goodhart's law, Campbell's law and reactive measures
topics.summary: Why a measure used as a target loses its informational value, from monetary policy and evaluation research to multitask incentive theory and public-sector targets.

claims.title: Problems of Monetary Management: The U.K. Experience
claims.venue: Papers in Monetary Economics, Reserve Bank of Australia
claims.rationale: Origin of Goodhart's law: any observed statistical regularity collapses once pressure is placed on it for control purposes.

claims.title: Assessing the impact of planned social change
claims.rationale: Campbell's law: the more a social indicator is used for decision-making, the more it is corrupted and distorts the process it monitors.

claims.title: Multitask Principal-Agent Analyses: Incentive Contracts, Asset Ownership, and Job Design
claims.venue: Journal of Law, Economics, and Organization
claims.rationale: The formal model of effort substitution toward measured tasks; the economic microfoundation for why rewarding an indicator distorts behaviour.

claims.title: What's measured is what matters: targets and gaming in the English public health care system
claims.rationale: Empirical taxonomy of gaming responses (ratchet, threshold, output distortion) to performance targets; a template for diagnosing indicator distortion.

topics.label: Rankings, benchmarking and indicators as governance
topics.summary: How cross-country indices and rankings exert pressure on governments, how they reshape what they measure, and how much their rank orderings can be trusted.

claims.title: Rankings and Reactivity: How Public Measures Recreate Social Worlds
claims.rationale: The sociological theory of reactivity: rankings change the organisations they rank through self-fulfilling prophecy and commensuration.

claims.title: Indicators as a Technology of Global Governance
claims.rationale: Frames global indicators as governance tools that embed theories and shift power to their producers; the standard reference in the indicators-and-governance literature.

claims.title: Introduction: The Power of Global Performance Indicators
claims.rationale: Introduces the special issue on global performance indicators with a theory of how they work through social pressure and domestic politics.

claims.title: The Power of Ranking: The Ease of Doing Business Indicator and Global Regulatory Behavior
claims.rationale: Causal evidence that a widely-used ranking induces governments to reform the measured items; a Goodhart effect at the country level.

claims.title: The tyranny of international index rankings
claims.rationale: Shows that rank uncertainty in the HDI, Doing Business and similar indices is large enough that most published rank differences are statistically meaningless.
